purpose: Living architectural/design/theoretical/quality findings for a major refactoring phase after frontend parity. Record during every rewrite/port slice; do not expand current scope automatically.

policy.required_handoff: Update existing entry or add one with evidence, impact, current workaround, later proposal and validation; explicitly record none observed when applicable.
policy.certainty: Separate confirmed defect/limitation, supported design risk and hypothesis. Missing frontend implementation alone is not poor architecture.
policy.timing: Fix required behavior/contract correctness in current slice; defer broader structural cleanup. Never use deferred status to waive a frontend acceptance gate.
policy.deduplication: Stable RF IDs, append new evidence and affected workflows rather than duplicate entries.
policy.closure: Retain history with fix/decision/source/evidence; do not delete embarrassing findings or mark solved from a plan.

findings.title: Shared presentation and Runtime are integration hotspots
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: At recorded baseline c827c4e6, the presentation spanned 1,399 lines and Runtime 960 lines, with shell, workspace routing, data/service actions and lifecycle integration sharing these modules; the reference Workbench was 1,426 lines. These are historical measurements, not current line counts. Length alone is not a defect; the concrete cost is that independent workflow edits repeatedly touch the same ownership surface.
findings.impact: Concurrent changes can conflict, and a one-to-one port could preserve broad coupling between workspace controls and service lifecycles.
findings.during_port: Use private feature modules with one coordinator owning shared composition; avoid a general framework before useful screens land.
findings.post_port_proposal: After parity, assess stable workspace/host orchestration modules with narrow interfaces and one authoritative session.
findings.validation_needed: Measure cross-workflow files changed for a representative feature and show that isolated workflow edits/tests no longer require unrelated shell/runtime changes.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry

findings.title: Internal browser host types are exposed as crate APIs
findings.confidence: confirmed observation; future cost is a design risk
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: web exports cad_jobs, renderer_host and several host modules publicly; CadOperation/CadRequest and wrapper methods are public. Adding a seemingly internal operation can therefore widen a Rust crate surface even when wire/file semantics stay unchanged. The page binary separately declares Runtime/presentation and imports the boardstudio_web library: pub(crate) in that library is not callable from the binary. Private wrapper placement must account for the actual crate boundary.
findings.impact: Implementation detail and intentional compatibility contract are hard to distinguish; private adapter evolution can trigger unnecessary broad API decisions.
findings.during_port: Place a private wrapper in the same crate as its consumer, or use an already sufficient public facade. Verify library-to-binary reachability before declaring a pub(crate) wrapper feasible; any needed public expansion remains an explicit decision.
findings.post_port_proposal: Audit actual consumers, explicitly separate stable public contracts from host internals, and propose compatible deprecation/module boundaries rather than silently shrinking visibility.
findings.validation_needed: List real external consumers and compile compatibility fixtures; prove internal operation changes no longer alter the intended public surface.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry
findings.follow_up_owner: post-port refactoring triage; discovering workflow maintains evidence

findings.title: Immutable export tokens do not model export-owned commits
findings.confidence: confirmed contract mismatch for PCB workflow
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Session export captures an immutable token and cancels registered exports on accepted commits. React PCB export deliberately adopts its own wiring and protection commits, with packaging before protection, while unrelated changes invalidate output.
findings.impact: A naive port either cancels its own valid export or weakens stale-output guards. Ownership of a multi-step operation and its accepted document lineage is not represented uniformly.

findings.validation_needed: Race matrix: owned versus unrelated commits, save failure, navigation, cancellation and packaging failure; no stale delivery and no protection without successful packaging.

findings.title: Geometric edit planning lives in frontend helper policy
findings.confidence: confirmed remaining TS policy; target placement is a hypothesis
findings.status: observed; structural proposal deferred until post-port review
findings.observation: Resize/reflow computes canonical linked-half deduplication, axis projections, spacing and center preservation in TS UI helpers. No equivalent callable Rust resize/reflow controller was found, although core owns matrix projection and accepted edits. The pinned React Case edit path also plans generated PCB clearance parts from canonical and physical-instance closure settings: it reflects flipped X coordinates, deduplicates board/position holes while preserving the largest required drill, replaces only its owned generated parts/definitions, and synchronizes layout and board membership. Rust SetMechanical only assigns doc.mechanical; it does not perform this document projection.
findings.impact: A component-only rewrite would lose behavior or leave hidden TS logic; moving the policy carelessly could duplicate geometry authority. A Case configuration-only port would also leave exported PCB holes and saved membership stale, while splitting the update into separate edits would break atomic Undo/persistence behavior.
findings.during_port: F6C.3 ports the existing policy into a private Rust frontend controller with preserved helper/public workflow tests and one normal edit/history path. F7.4e preserves the bounded Case closure-clearance document projection through one existing accepted-document/Session edit, without moving geometry authority or widening public APIs.
findings.post_port_proposal: After parity, decide whether interaction planning belongs in a dedicated application service using core geometry primitives, with explicit draft/commit ownership.
findings.validation_needed: Compare identical resize traces across pointer/keyboard, mixed selections and linked boards; no semantic drift, duplicated calculations or extra history steps. For Case, compare canonical/physical-instance closure edits, reflected and coincident holes, generated definition/drill data, board/layout membership, saved archive payload, one-step Undo/Redo and reopen.
findings.decision: proposal only; no refactor/API/schema change approved by this entry

findings.impact: A single cancelled status can obscure remaining CPU/memory work or lead the UI to promise prompt preemption that the engine does not provide.

findings.validation_needed: Measure cancel-to-settle and retained resources for queued, chunked preview and synchronous export; verify no stale scene/file even when computation finishes after cancellation.

findings.title: Object tree containers have invalid required-child semantics
findings.confidence: confirmed inherited critical axe violation in the Dioxus candidate and pinned React reference
findings.status: open; no accessibility waiver; candidate acceptance gate remains required; private semantics repair f65b is under independent review and is not integrated or accepted
findings.observation: Axe 4.12.1 reports the critical aria-required-children violation in both paired applications: the candidate .m1-component-list role=tree directly contains labelled disclosure buttons, and the React .wb-tree-viewport role=tree has the same invalid child pattern. The candidate report has one critical violation; the React report has the same critical violation plus a separate moderate page-has-heading-one finding. The shared result identifies an inherited reference defect; it does not establish candidate conformance or waive accessibility acceptance. A private candidate semantics repair exists at f65b and is under independent review; it is neither merged nor accepted and does not close this finding.
findings.impact: Assistive technologies may not receive the required tree/treeitem structure for object hierarchy navigation. The axe impact is critical and remains an active correctness gate.
findings.during_port: Do not suppress the rule, weaken the threshold or accept the candidate because the reference shares the defect. Correct candidate tree semantics while preserving hierarchy, selection and keyboard behavior; retain both reports as paired baseline evidence. Actual assistive-technology testing remains separately required where applicable.
findings.post_port_proposal: Review the tree semantic structure and maintained accessibility conformance scenario across workspace navigation; keep the eventual design narrow and compatible with tree disclosure and selection behavior.
findings.validation_needed: Axe reports no aria-required-children violation on the candidate; public hierarchy, selection, keyboard and focus behavior remain correct; retain the React report as evidence of the inherited baseline defect. Actual assistive-technology evidence is a separate gate.
